messages.subject: Power Analysis - R code
parts:
I am working on a power analysis for detecting a change between two abund=
ance estimates using a z-test

z =3D (N1-N2)/sgrt(var(N1-N2))

I have wrote the following R code to estimate power:

ZPOWER.2sided =3D function(change,N1,CV,alpha){
N2=3DN1+(N1*change)
SD1=3DN1*CV
SD2=3DN2*CV
VAR=3D(SD1^2)+(SD2^2)
qL=3Dqnorm(alpha/2)
qU=3Dqnorm(1-(alpha/2))
Z =3D(N1-N2)/sqrt(VAR)
power =3D (pnorm(qL-Z))+(1-pnorm(qU-Z))
cbind(N1,N2,change,CV,SD1,SD2,VAR,qL,qU,Z,alpha,power)}
# Where N1 and N2 are the two abundances, change is the desired percent c=
hange, and CV is coefficient of var.

# Example use of function.
ZPOWER.2sided(change=3D-0.2,N1=3D300,CV=3D0.15,alpha=3D0.05)

After writing this code, I found the following code posted at http://www.=
creem.st-and.ac.uk/len/software.html.

#--------------------------------------------
#Power to detect a change between two time
# points using a z-test. Not used in book
# chapter
#--------------------------------------------
#alpha level (type I error)
alpha<-0.05=20
#vector of coefficients of var
cvs <- seq(0.05,0.5,by=3D0.05)=20
#vector of true differences
fs <- seq(0,1,by=3D0.1)
lcvs<-length(cvs)
lfs<-length(fs)
res<-matrix(0,lcvs,lfs)
q1<-qnorm(1-(alpha/2))
q2<-qnorm(alpha/2)
s2<-sqrt(2)
#work out power at each level of CV and true diff
for(i1 in 1:lcvs) {
cv<-cvs[i1]
for (i2 in 1:lfs) {
f<-fs[i2]
z<-f/(s2*cv)
power =3D (1-pnorm(q1-z)) + pnorm(q2 - z)
res[i1,i2]<-power
}
}
#output as a perspective plot
persp(cvs,fs,res)
#--------------------------------------------


A major difference between my code and this code is z=3D(N1-N2)/sqrt(VAR)=
vs. z=3Df/(s2*cv).

Can someone help me understand the use of sqrt(2)*CV in the denomiator in=
stead of sqrt(VAR)?

Thanks,

Matt
